latin: De potentia dei absoluta possibile est culpam originalem deleri sine infusione gratiae.
translation: By the absolute power of God it is possible for original guilt to be erased without the infusion of grace.
translation_note: 'Culpam originalem': original guilt, that is, original sin considered as culpability rather than as the resulting corruption of nature (farmer1998:12258).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch6, from Latin at farmer1998:12258

sources.text: John Duns Scotus, Ordinatio 4, d. 1, pars 4, q. 1 (Opera omnia, vol. 11, Vatican City, 2008, pp. 122–131)
sources.pico_relation: Edelheit identifies this question, where Scotus rejects Richard of Middleton's opposing view, as the source of thesis 13

doctrine: The thesis concerns the scope of God's absolute power (potentia dei absoluta) in relation to sin and grace: whether original guilt could, in principle, be removed without the accompanying infusion of sanctifying grace (farmer1998:12258). Edelheit states that according to thesis 13 it is possible, by the absolute power of God, for original sin to be eliminated without the infusion of grace, and locates the discussion in Scotus's Ordinatio, book 4, distinction 1, part 4, question 1, where Scotus first presents and rejects an opposing view of Richard of Middleton before arguing his own position (edelheit2022:14519).
historiography: No Farmer note on thesis 13 is recorded in the material consulted, and Edelheit's identification of the Ordinatio passage, with its reference to Richard of Middleton's rejected view, is the only scholarly treatment available (edelheit2022:14519).

quotations.text: it is possible, thanks to the absolute power of God, for the Original Sin to be eliminated without the infusion of grace

not_established: Whether Pico endorses or merely reports this Scotist position is not addressed by Edelheit in the material consulted; no Farmer note on the thesis is recorded in the packet.
